inputs.source: Customer email body received as a new support ticket

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id, not limited to an account matching the ticket requester, enabling cross-customer data access if an account id is referenced or asserted in the inbound email.
The only defense against disclosing another customer's information is a prompt instruction, not a structural check binding the looked-up account to the sender's verified identity.
'Routine' and 'angry' are undefined; the model alone decides whether to send autonomously or escalate, so escalation is a judgment call rather than a defined boundary.
No structural approval gate exists for outbound email containing confidential data; the decision to send directly is entirely a model judgment call with no human checkpoint by default.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to comply; a more capable model, a longer conversation, or an injected instruction in the untrusted email body can produce a rationalized exception.

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside the model and does not decay with model capability, but it only records the event after the email has already been sent; it does not prevent disclosure.

controls.name: Bind CRM lookup to the requester's own verified account
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the CRM integration layer rather than by model choice; remains effective regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Bind outbound email destination to the ticket's verified requester address from the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: The destination would come from the ticketing system record rather than model-chosen text, so it does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Scope CRM and mail service tokens to least privilege per ticket
controls.decay_rationale: A narrowly scoped credential limits blast radius independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action review) before sending emails containing customer PII
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action human approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not decay with model capability, though it can be removed by autonomy increases or weakened by approval fatigue at high volume.

controls.name: Pin and hash crm_mcp and mail_mcp tool definitions
controls.decay_rationale: Definition pinning is enforced by the client at connection time, independent of model behavior.

findings.title: TC1: Lethal trifecta — untrusted email drives unrestricted CRM lookup and autonomous send of confidential customer data

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email; may reference any account id or impersonate another customer
Agent looks up any customer by email or account id (prompt.md:3), returning confidential account data regardless of match to sender
Agent sends the drafted reply directly using a shared mail service account that can send to any address, with no human approval or destination check

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model provider or version string changes in the deployment config (subject.model.swappable=true, upgraded with the platform with no separate review); treat any such change as requiring reassessment before it handles live tickets.

evidence.observation: The agent looks up the customer's account with get_customer and 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' not limited to an account matching the sender.
Routine responses are sent directly with send; the only condition for pausing is the model's own judgment that the customer is 'angry,' which is not a structural gate.
The sole defense against cross-customer disclosure is a single prompt instruction, a behavioral and capability-dependent control.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are authenticated with static bearer tokens; no per-request or per-customer scoping is declared.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Bind CRM lookups to the account associated with the ticket requester's authenticated identity; block or escalate lookups of any other account id referenced in the email body.

Add a raw-action human approval gate for outbound emails containing confidential customer data, or restrict the send tool's destination to the verified requester address pulled from the ticket record.
Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN to least privilege (per-session or per-ticket) rather than full-database read and any-address send.
Alert when an outbound email's recipient does not match the ticket's originating sender, supplementing the existing SIEM log.

findings.title: ASI04: Unpinned crm_mcp and mail_mcp tool definitions permit a silent rug pull

attack_path.note: crm_mcp tool definition is not declared as pinned or hashed
mail_mcp tool definition is not declared as pinned or hashed

evidence.observation: No version pin, hash, or lock mechanism is declared for the crm_mcp or mail_mcp tool definitions; the config only supplies a URL and bearer token.

recommendations.action: Pin and hash tool definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp; verify the hash on every session start and alert on drift.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted email (U) can drive a read of confidential CRM data across any customer account and an irreversible send through a shared mail credential to any address (S3 sink), the highest cell in the base matrix. The only present preventive control is a single behavioral, capability-dependent prompt instruction ('never share another customer's information'), which under rubric section 5 step 4 earns exactly one tier of credit, giving a residual of high. Detective SIEM logging earns no tier credit because it only records the event after the email has already been sent. No structural control (account binding, destination binding, scoped credentials, or human approval) currently exists to sever or narrow the path. Under the model_upgrade trigger, the one present control decays further because prompt instructions are classified dependent and fail under model_upgrade, and the model is explicitly upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so the forecast returns to critical. A secondary finding on unpinned MCP tool definitions contributes a stable high risk with no present controls. Overall forecast equals the maximum of all findings' residual and projected risk: critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest or JSON schema for crm_mcp.get_customer or mail_mcp.send was provided; capability scope is inferred from the prompt instruction 'You may look up any customer by email or account id,' which lowers confidence on the exact API surface.
No agent card, IaC, or source code was provided; autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are undeclared and are treated as null rather than verified.
The system prompt was truncated after line 14 ('...'); additional directives beyond the shown lines were not available for review and could raise or lower the rating.
